intro: STL to X3D converts STL models to X3D on the server, with nothing to install. It is useful, for example, to publish a part in an X3D web viewer or a repository that uses the standard. X3D is VRML's successor, an ISO standard in XML opened by MeshLab, Blender, X3DOM web viewers and many scientific and heritage programs.

STL is the format every slicer reads: it only stores triangles, with no units or colours. X3D uses the Y axis up, so the STL model, with Z up as in 3D printing, is turned so it stands upright; the advanced options let you keep the axes. Choose the units of the STL and the X3D.

The X3D comes out in XML with one shape per part, its coordinates and, if there are colours, one colour per face. You can apply a scale and keep the STL parts separate, merge them or get one per file in a ZIP.

The STL geometry is not simplified or repaired on its way to X3D. Up to one million triangles are accepted without an account, two million with a free account and ten million with Pro, and up to ten files per task. Each file is converted in an isolated process on our server in the European Union and deleted when it expires.
steps: Upload one or more STL files.
Choose the units and, optionally, the scale and parts.

faq.q: Why does the X3D come out lying down?
faq.a: Because STL and X3D do not use the same vertical axis. Tick or untick “Keep the original axes” in the advanced options.
Yes when the X3D supports them (VRML, X3D and USDZ); STL stores no colours and the note says so.

faq.q: What if the STL has textures?
faq.a: STL textures are not converted: the geometry and each face's or material's colour go through.
